title: Lesson factory runner log record
description: One line a factory runner may emit. Logs are the surface where protected material leaks most easily, because a log line looks harmless and is written in a hurry: rubric §7.3 names logs alongside handoffs and diagnostics as a place protected keys, scoring material, and private rationale must never appear. This contract makes that structural rather than advisory. A record carries an enumerated event code, opaque identifiers, hash references, and integer counts. It carries no free text at all, so there is no field in which a key, an accepted response, a rationale, a secret, or a serialised payload could travel.
$comment: Every string this record admits is an enum member, a fixed-shape identifier, a hex digest, or a timestamp. Nothing here references NonEmptyString, and nothing here uses the general-purpose reference and blocker types either: their locators admit dots, slashes, and hyphenated words, so `blocker:the-answer-is-c` and `lesson:the-answer-is-c#sha256:...` both match them. A log gets its own narrower types so an identifier cannot be used as a sentence.

contract_version.description: The one contract version this schema describes. An instance that claims another version was validated against a contract that is not this one.

lesson_ref.description: The exact revision a line is about, as a lesson id, a revision number, and a hash — nothing else fits the shape. A bare lesson id is not accepted either: two retired preview lessons reused production ids (rubric §9.1), so an id in a log names an ambiguous thing.

blocker_code.description: Why something is blocked, from a closed list. The general blocker type is a pattern over slugs, which any runtime-invented string can satisfy; an enum can only hold a reason someone added deliberately.

counts.description: Aggregates only. A count of failures is safe to log; the thing that failed is not.

protected_items_referenced.description: How many protected items a stage touched. The count is loggable; the items are not.

hashes.description: Opaque digests, which identify bytes without disclosing them. The key set is closed, so a runner cannot invent a hash-shaped field and put something else in it.

redaction.description: The record states its own transport rules, so a line that tried to opt out of them would be rejected by the same contract that validates it.
